title: Outdoor Holiday Cookie Decorating: Baking on a Grill Mat
meta_description: Move the mess outside! Learn how to use a holiday cookies grill mat to bake festive treats on your BBQ without the oven heat or sticky pans.
html:
When the holiday season hits, the kitchen usually becomes a war zone of flour, sprinkles, and competing timers. If you’re like me, you love the tradition of baking, but you hate the heat of a preheated oven making your house feel like a sauna in December. That’s why I’ve started moving a portion of my baking operation outdoors.

Using a holiday cookies grill mat is a game-changer for anyone who wants to reclaim their kitchen counter space. By utilizing your outdoor grill as a makeshift oven, you can bake batches of sugar cookies or gingerbread while the main meal simmers inside. The secret is using high-quality BBQ Grill Mats to ensure your cookies don't fall through the grates or succumb to a sudden flare-up.

Setting Up Your Outdoor Baking Station

Before you fire up the grill, you need to treat it like an oven. Most gas grills have a lid, which is essential for trapping heat. To get a consistent bake, I recommend using an indirect heat method. Light the burners on one side of the grill and leave the other side off, or use a warming rack if your grill has one.

Place your BBQ Grill Mats on the cooler side of the grate. Because these mats are non-stick and reusable, you don't have to worry about greasing them with butter or lining them with parchment paper that might blow away in a light breeze. Just place your cut-out dough directly onto the mat.

Why Use BBQ Grill Mats for Baking?

You might be wondering why you wouldn't just use a standard baking sheet on the grill. I've tried it, and it's clunky. Baking sheets often warp under the intense, uneven heat of a grill, and they don't distribute heat as evenly as a specialized mat.

The BBQ Grill Mats are designed to handle high temperatures while preventing sticking. This is crucial for delicate holiday cookies that have high butter content. Since the mats create a barrier, you avoid those charred grill marks on the bottom of your shortbread, giving you a clean, golden-brown finish that looks like it came from a professional bakery.

Tips for Perfect Holiday Cookies on a Grill Mat

Baking outdoors requires a few adjustments to your standard indoor routine. Since you can't always peek through a glass oven door, you'll need to be a bit more strategic about your timing. Here are a few tips to ensure your treats turn out perfectly:

  • Check Your Temp: Use an external grill thermometer to ensure your surface temperature stays between 325°F and 350°F.
  • Chill Your Dough: Cold dough holds its shape better on a grill mat, preventing the cookies from spreading too much.
  • Rotate Early: About halfway through the baking time, gently rotate the mat or the cookies to account for any hot spots in your grill.
  • Keep the Lid Closed: Every time you lift the lid, you lose a significant amount of heat, which can lead to uneven baking.

Decorating Your Outdoor Holiday Cookies

The best part about moving the baking outside is that you can set up a massive decorating station on your patio table. Once your cookies have cooled on the BBQ Grill Mats, move them to a large platter.

I love setting up a "decorating assembly line" with bowls of royal icing, festive sprinkles, and small candies. Because the baking happened outdoors, your indoor dining table remains a crumb-free zone for guests. If you're working with kids, this is the perfect way to let them go wild with the sprinkles without worrying about flour getting into your indoor upholstery.

Cleaning Up After the Bake

One of the biggest hurdles to outdoor baking is the cleanup. However, utilizing a holiday cookies grill mat makes this process nearly instant. Instead of scrubbing a burnt baking sheet in the sink, you simply wipe down the non-stick surface of the BBQ Grill Mats.

For heavier residue, like leaked jam or melted chocolate, these mats can usually be washed with warm soapy water. Once they are dry, they can be stored flat and kept ready for your next batch of seasonal treats, whether it's Christmas cookies or springtime macarons.

FAQ

Can I use any grill for this method?

Yes, as long as your grill has a lid to trap heat. Gas grills are generally easier to regulate, but charcoal grills work as well, provided you push the coals to one side to create a zone of indirect heat.

Will my cookies taste like smoke?

If you use BBQ Grill Mats, the barrier prevents the cookies from coming into direct contact with the grates and minimizes smoke absorption. To ensure a clean taste, make sure your grill is cleaned of old grease before you start baking.

How many cookies can I fit on one mat?

This depends on the size of your mat and the size of your cookies. Just be sure to leave at least two inches between each cookie to allow the heat to circulate, ensuring an even bake across the entire surface.
